dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The current site presents Nick primarily as a general TypeScript/DX community figure, so technical leaders cannot quickly see his current AI-native DX leadership or a credible path to workshops.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: The redesign must establish AI-native DX authority within the first viewport, make workshops the primary next step, unify the perception-shaping pages, and preserve the public archive.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Success is defined by runnable typecheck/build/route checks plus named human review of the five-second message, visual authorship, theme readability, and responsive hierarchy.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Scope includes the shared system and key perception-shaping pages while explicitly excluding article rewrites, every experimental route, a CMS, fabricated claims, and a visual clone of Zack Proser’s site.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: AI-native DX authority is the primary message, workshops are the primary action, and writing, speaking, projects, streaming, and prior community work consistently serve as evidence rather than competing identities.

problem: Technical leaders arriving at nicknisi.com encounter a visually energetic but dated positioning system that still describes Nick mainly as a TypeScript enthusiast, conference organizer, streamer, and developer experience engineer. That framing understates his current leadership and hands-on work in AI-native developer experience, so visitors evaluating workshops, speaking, or collaboration must assemble the relevant story themselves.

The site already contains substantial proof through writing, talks, projects, conference material, and workshop participation, but the homepage and key routes do not organize that evidence into a clear authority narrative or provide a Nick-owned workshop destination. A fresh visual system must change that perception without sacrificing the archive, readability, personality, or existing URLs.
goals: Make a first-time technical leader understand within one viewport that Nick Nisi works at the intersection of AI adoption, developer experience, and engineering practice.
Make exploring workshops the homepage’s primary next step while keeping writing, speaking, projects, and community work visible as authority evidence.
Create a Nick-centered workshops page that accurately explains his role in the shared Claude workshop collaboration and routes qualified visitors to the verified shared booking destination.
Replace the shared visual system and perception-shaping routes with one responsive, accessible, unmistakably Nick design selected and executed through the Impeccable workflow.
Preserve the existing Astro content archive, public URLs, and long-form readability while updating stale positioning and metadata.

successCriteria.criterion: The project typechecks after the redesign.
The production site builds after the redesign.
The production build includes the redesigned homepage, workshops page, about page, speaking page, writing index, and a representative article.

check.cmd: test -f dist/index.html && test -f dist/workshops/index.html && test -f dist/about/index.html && test -f dist/speaking/index.html && test -f dist/posts/index.html && test -f dist/posts/ai-tooling/index.html

successCriteria.criterion: The homepage and workshops page expose stable structural markers for their primary jobs rather than relying on copy-sensitive verification.
The legacy AI engineering route continues to resolve to the new workshop destination.
A five-second review communicates Nick’s name, AI-native DX focus, credible evidence, and the workshops path without requiring scrolling.

check.judgment: Nick reviews the desktop and mobile first viewports and can identify all four elements within five seconds.

successCriteria.criterion: The visual system feels specifically authored for Nick rather than like a generic AI/SaaS portfolio or a visual imitation of Zack Proser’s site.

check.judgment: Nick compares the final desktop and mobile screenshots against the approved Impeccable direction and the Zack reference, confirming distinct authorship.

successCriteria.criterion: Light and dark themes remain readable and intentional across the homepage, workshops page, article index, and representative article at desktop and mobile widths.

check.judgment: The Impeccable finish review inspects paired light/dark desktop/mobile screenshots and reports no unresolved material contrast, hierarchy, overflow, or theme-inversion defects.

successCriteria.criterion: The workshops page makes only source-backed claims about Nick, the crew, workshop format, and booking path.

check.judgment: Nick verifies the page against the existing site content and Zack Proser workshop source before approval; no invented clients, outcomes, pricing, availability, or testimonials remain.

mvp.item: Durable product record and Impeccable visual-direction process
mvp.reason: The redesign needs confirmed product truth and an approved visual world before implementation; competitor imitation or another arbitrary reskin would repeat the current problem.

mvp.item: Shared visual foundation and global chrome
mvp.reason: Typography, color, spacing, surfaces, navigation, footer, theme behavior, focus states, and responsive rules must establish one coherent system across the archive.
The homepage is the main perception problem and must establish AI-native DX authority, proof, and workshops as the primary action.
Nick needs a durable home for his role in the shared workshop offer and a clear route to the verified booking flow.

mvp.item: Preserved archive and legacy route continuity
mvp.reason: The redesign cannot break existing article URLs or the current AI engineering entry point.

full.item: About page and reusable press-kit repositioning
full.reason: Bios and personal context must align with current AI-native DX leadership while keeping past podcast and wedding details appropriately secondary.

full.item: Speaking page and core content indexes
full.reason: These routes provide the strongest supporting evidence and should inherit the new hierarchy rather than read as disconnected archives.
Articles are major entry points and need the new typography, navigation, themes, and authority context without rewriting individual posts.

full.item: Metadata, descriptions, navigation, and social-preview positioning
full.reason: Search and shared links must communicate the same current identity as the rendered pages.
Typed Void should remain the legal/business vehicle and send visitors to Nick’s canonical workshop destination rather than maintain a competing public brand.

stretch.item: Selective motion or signature interaction from the approved Impeccable direction
stretch.reason: A memorable interaction can strengthen authorship only after clarity, accessibility, responsiveness, and performance are proven.

stretch.item: Additional recent workshop and conference media curation
stretch.reason: Existing assets may support richer proof, but only verified, high-quality media that improves the narrative should be added.

outOfScope.reason: The archive is evidence and should inherit the new system; individual editorial rewrites do not serve the positioning goal.

outOfScope.item: Individually redesigning every experiment, utility, résumé, and specialty route
outOfScope.reason: Core-system inheritance is sufficient; bespoke work on every route would expand cost without improving the primary audience journey.

outOfScope.item: A separate Typed Void visual identity or full website
outOfScope.reason: Nick is the public brand; maintaining two full brand systems would split attention and credibility.

outOfScope.item: A visual clone of Zack Proser’s site
outOfScope.reason: His hierarchy and proof strategy are useful references, but the result must be unmistakably Nick and use an independently chosen Impeccable direction.

outOfScope.item: A CMS, newsletter platform, analytics program, or lead-management system
outOfScope.reason: None is required to solve the current positioning and design problem.

outOfScope.item: Invented testimonials, clients, outcomes, prices, availability, or performance claims
outOfScope.reason: Commercial credibility must come from verified evidence, not placeholder social proof.

future: Measure workshop-path usage after launch and decide whether a newsletter or broader work-with-me funnel earns prominence.
Revisit specialty routes only when traffic or content importance justifies bespoke treatment.
Add case studies when verified client or workshop outcomes are available and approved for publication.

decisions.decision: Use nicknisi.com as the canonical public brand and keep Typed Void LLC as the legal/business vehicle.
decisions.rejected: Maintain and redesign separate Nick Nisi and Typed Void public brands.
decisions.reason: Clients hire Nick’s reputation and expertise; two public brands would split maintenance, SEO, and credibility.

decisions.rejected: Turn the homepage into a workshop-first sales funnel.
decisions.reason: The site must remain a durable personal authority hub whose commercial path is credible because of the work around it.

decisions.decision: Position Nick around AI-native developer experience for technical leaders.
decisions.rejected: Lead with generic AI expertise, developer tooling alone, or technical education alone.
decisions.reason: AI-native DX connects Nick’s current leadership, engineering systems, tooling history, and teaching without erasing the foundation that differentiates him.

decisions.decision: Create a Nick-centered workshops page with a shared booking handoff.
decisions.rejected: Only link to Zack’s page or duplicate its complete sales page.
decisions.reason: Nick needs durable ownership of his role and evidence without creating two competing canonical descriptions of the offer.

decisions.decision: Redesign the core system and perception-shaping pages.
decisions.rejected: Redesign every generated route or limit work to homepage styling.
decisions.reason: This changes the visitor’s perception coherently while preserving the archive and avoiding another expensive whole-site churn.

decisions.decision: Use Impeccable to select and execute the visual world.
decisions.rejected: Copy Zack Proser’s visual identity or silently continue the incumbent zine system.
decisions.reason: The result must meet a high craft bar and feel specifically authored for Nick rather than competitor-derived or merely polished.

execution.strategy: Sequential design lock followed by coordinated implementation and bounded finish review

phases.title: Visual Direction and System
phases.notes: Run the Impeccable direction and composition process, approve the visual world, and implement the shared foundation, chrome, themes, and responsive rules.

phases.title: Authority and Workshops Journey
phases.notes: Build the authority-led homepage, Nick-centered workshops page, verified booking handoff, legacy route continuity, and supporting media.

phases.title: Evidence Surfaces and Archive Integration
phases.notes: Align about, press kit, speaking, indexes, article layout, metadata, navigation, and Typed Void redirect destination with the approved positioning and system.

phases.title: Impeccable Finish Review
phases.notes: Inspect desktop/mobile and light/dark in bounded passes, run the design detector, complete an independent finish review, resolve material findings, and record DESIGN.md from the shipped system.
